extracted.intended_audience: school administrators, Title IX coordinators, athletic associations, state policymakers, institutional legal counsel, and other stakeholders on Title IX athletics policy
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and regulatory standards for when and how recipients of federal funds may adopt or apply sex-related eligibility criteria for participation on male or female athletic teams, especially as they affect transgender, intersex, and nonbinary students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate teams permitted when based on competitive skill or contact sport
rubrics_metrics.description: Current §106.41(b) permits a recipient to offer separate male and female athletic teams when selection for such teams is based upon competitive skill or the activity involved is a contact sport.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (b) also states that when a recipient operates or sponsors a team in a particular sport for members of one sex but operates or sponsors no such team for members of the excluded sex, and athletic opportunities for members of the excluded sex have previously been limited, members of the excluded sex must be allowed to try out for the team offered unless the sport involved is a contact sport. The regulation recognizes that individual students may be denied participation on a particular team on the basis of sex in some instances, provided overall equal opportunity is preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall equal athletic opportunity requirement (§106.41(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide equal opportunity in its athletic program as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient that excludes a student from one team (e.g., excludes a boy from girls' golf where no boys' team exists) must ensure equal opportunity across the totality of its athletic program; disparities in overall participation opportunities across male and female teams could violate §106.41(c) depending on the facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Try-out requirement for excluded sex when no team exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a recipient operates a team in a sport for one sex but not the other and opportunities for the excluded sex were previously limited, members of the excluded sex must be allowed to try out for the team offered unless the sport is a contact sport.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of current §106.41(b)'s exception allowing some sex-separated teams while protecting access when one sex is excluded from a sport entirely; recipients should permit try-outs in such circumstances unless the sport is a contact sport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed standard for sex-related eligibility criteria (substantially related & minimize harms)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient adopts or applies sex-related criteria that would limit or deny a student's eligibility to participate on a male or female team consistent with their gender identity, such criteria must, for each sport, level of competition, and grade or education level, (i) be substantially related to the achievement of an important educational objective, and (ii) minimize harms to students whose opportunity to participate on a male or female team consistent with their gender identity would be limited or denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed regulation applies the standard per sport/level/grade and preserves that some sex-related distinctions may be permissible so long as the recipient ensures overall equal opportunity. This is intended to provide clearer Title IX framework for analyzing eligibility criteria that affect transgender, intersex, and nonbinary students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid causing more than de minimis harm by separation or different treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed amendments would clarify that, in the limited circumstances Title IX permits different treatment or separation on the basis of sex, a recipient must not carry out such treatment in a manner that discriminates by subjecting a person to more than de minimis harm, unless otherwise permitted by Title IX or the Department's regulations; and a policy that prevents a person from participating consistent with their gender identity subjects that person to more than de minimis harm on the basis of sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle is intended to limit the manner in which permitted sex-separation can be implemented to avoid discriminatory harm in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility requirements must be age-appropriate, tailored, and evidence-based (medical/competitive safety)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responding to OCR guidance (2016 Dear Colleague Letter): Title IX does not prohibit age-appropriate, tailored requirements based on sound, current, and research-based medical knowledge about the impact of the students' participation on the competitive fairness or physical safety of the sport, but a recipient may not adopt requirements that rely on overly broad generalizations or stereotypes or others' discomfort with transgender students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility rules grounded in medical or safety considerations should be narrowly tailored, current, and research-based; policies based on generalized assumptions, stereotypes, or mere discomfort are impermissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply constitutional equal protection analysis as informative framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal courts' equal protection analysis (e.g., requirement that sex-based classifications serve important governmental objectives and be substantially related to achieving those objectives) provides a helpful framework for evaluating when certain sex-based classifications may be justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While Title IX's scope differs from the Equal Protection Clause, courts have used intermediate scrutiny concepts in reviewing laws/policies that classify on the basis of sex or transgender status; recipients and regulators should consider whether asserted objectives are important and whether the criteria are substantially related to those objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sport-, level-, and grade-specific assessment required
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed regulation requires that any sex-related criteria be evaluated for each sport, level of competition, and grade or education level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should not apply blanket, one-size-fits-all eligibility rules across all sports, levels, or grades; assessments must be specific to the competitive context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the nature of particular sports when crafting eligibility rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Congressional direction (Javits Amendment) permits the Department to adopt reasonable provisions considering the nature of particular sports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory and institutional rules should account for sport-specific characteristics (e.g., contact vs. non-contact, competitive structure) when determining what sex-related distinctions, if any, are reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor flexible compliance that expands student athletic opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR's longstanding policy encourages compliance with Title IX athletics regulation in a flexible manner that expands, rather than limits, student athletic opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In implementing eligibility criteria, recipients should prioritize program development and policies that increase participation opportunities for students (including historically underrepresented sexes) whenever feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate and minimize adverse impacts on intersex and nonbinary students
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts have not addressed Title IX's application to intersex or nonbinary student-athletes; the Department believes the proposed regulation provides an appropriate framework for analyzing criteria that limit or deny an intersex student's eligibility, and for nonbinary students a recipient may need to determine whether criteria limit or deny eligibility to participate on a male or female team consistent with their gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should examine whether eligibility criteria inadvertently exclude or disadvantage intersex or nonbinary students (e.g., via reliance on birth-assigned sex or binary markers) and take steps to minimize harms and ensure nondiscrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require evidence-based justification for categorical exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Court decisions (e.g., Hecox) have scrutinized categorical exclusions of transgender athletes and examined whether such policies actually advance important objectives; where legislative or policy bans lack evidence that they further equality or safety objectives, courts have found them likely violative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients adopting categorical bans or broad exclusions should be prepared to justify them with robust evidence showing the measures are substantially related to important objectives (e.g., equality of opportunity, safety), otherwise they risk legal challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess compliance by examining totality of athletic participation opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with Title IX athletics provisions requires examination of the totality of a recipient's athletic program — disparities in overall participation opportunities across sexes may indicate violations even if individual-team distinctions exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should look beyond single-team rules to measure whether the program as a whole provides equal athletic opportunities (including numbers of teams, roster spots, and program expansion), consistent with historical OCR guidance encouraging expansion of opportunities for underrepresented sexes.
